purpose: Design input for the Rust rewrite. Not executable configuration, a runtime installer manifest, or a Juiced support declaration.

priority_definitions.parity: Preserve the existing native recipe's selected product disposition and behavior. Native descriptors do not establish Rust or hardware qualification.
priority_definitions.first-expansion: Recommended first new integrations after shared catalog and worker contracts; additive to existing required scope. Every target still needs its own release decision and evidence.
priority_definitions.conditional: Add only for a named workload/device gap and selected-provider acceptance.
priority_definitions.attach: Connect to an explicitly configured independently owned service first. Lifecycle management must be separately negotiated.
priority_definitions.reference-only: Recognize packaging or client-local execution. No new daemon worker is proposed by this inventory.
priority_definitions.legacy: Recognize retained installations/artifacts without automatically creating new managed integrations.

candidate_backend_semantics: Candidate paths are research/design leads with per-entry constraints. Never construct an OS x backend x model Cartesian product, advertise them as qualified, or activate them from this file.

entries.name: llama.cpp
entries.notes: Initial managed builds preserve native CPU/CUDA/HIP/Vulkan/Metal scope. Other paths require separate build/model/platform qualification. Explicitly describe multimodal projectors and architecture coverage.

entries.name: llama.cpp XDNA hybrid distribution
entries.notes: Retain legacy llamacpp/hybrid-rocm as its pinned Nulifyer/llama-xdna-hybrid distribution and explicit NPU/GPU placement. Do not reinterpret it as ordinary upstream llama.cpp HIP.

entries.name: llama.cpp HRX distribution
entries.notes: Preserve recipe llamacpp-hrx, its exact fork/build and Linux gfx1100/gfx1151 restrictions. HRX is distribution-specific, not a hardware class.

entries.name: DwarfStar4 / ds4
entries.notes: Preserve the selected Linux gfx1151 package and curated model restrictions. Do not treat arbitrary GGUF as compatible.

entries.name: FastFlowLM
entries.notes: Native parity keeps published XDNA2 packages and existing operations. New modalities are upstream discovery claims until an adapter supports them.

entries.name: AMD Ryzen AI OGA stack
entries.notes: Keep native recipe ryzenai-llm. Distinguish NPU-only and NPU+iGPU hybrid profiles, exact prepared artifacts, vendor OGA versions and OS restrictions.

entries.name: whisper.cpp
entries.notes: Preserve native cpu/metal/npu/rocm/vulkan packaging first. CUDA and other upstream paths are additions. Core ML/OpenVINO/VitisAI acceleration can cover only selected stages.

entries.name: FUTO transcribe.cpp ASR4ALL worker
entries.notes: Pinned FUTO GitLab project. Native worker forces CPU and ASR4ALL architecture. Keep separate from handy-computer/transcribe.cpp despite the shared project name.

entries.name: Parakeet Redux / parakeet.cpp
entries.notes: Native container pins mudler/parakeet.cpp. Preserve the selected CPU worker and bounded WAV contract, independently of the Parakeet model family.

entries.name: Moonshine Voice
entries.notes: Preserve native moonshine CPU worker first. Current upstream toolkit and model revisions need their own adapter/version qualification.

entries.name: Kokoros native Kokoro worker
entries.notes: Native recipe kokoro downloads lemonade-sdk/Kokoros. Model family Kokoro does not identify this implementation.

entries.name: ONNX Runtime
entries.notes: Preserve existing CPU worker scope. Every additional provider and model pipeline needs an explicit worker, export/companion contract and selected operation.

entries.name: stable-diffusion.cpp
entries.notes: Preserve native sd-cpp cpu/cuda/rocm/vulkan/metal scope. Candidate video and extra backend support does not establish Juiced protocol support.

entries.name: TheNoise worker
entries.notes: Preserve packaged ROCm worker. Represent PyTorch and compiler-cache dependencies in its bundle identity, not a second independent resource reservation.

entries.name: OpenMOSS TTS worker
entries.notes: Preserve selected pwilkin/openmoss package, checkpoints and voice-design behavior as bounded native operations.

entries.name: ACE-Step C++ worker
entries.notes: Keep multi-checkpoint acquisition and async-job/cancellation requirements. Fixed music service does not authorize arbitrary graphs.

entries.name: ThinkSound C++ worker
entries.notes: Preserve selected native provider, artifacts and operations without assuming every upstream model is supported.

entries.name: TRELLIS.2 C++ worker
entries.notes: Carry selected existing 3D service scope. Native descriptor presence alone does not change conditional product disposition.

entries.name: vLLM
entries.notes: Preserve native ROCm package. CUDA/CPU/XPU additions and Metal/TPU/Ascend plugins are separate bundles and qualification cells.

entries.name: ik_llama.cpp
entries.notes: Independent fork identity and quantization coverage. Current upstream only calls CPU and CUDA fully functional and performant.

entries.name: MLX-LM
entries.notes: First target Apple Silicon Metal. Linux CPU/CUDA packages remain independent follow-on cells.

entries.name: SGLang
entries.notes: Start one exact CUDA or ROCm text-serving target. Other accelerators and diffusion require separate operation suites.

entries.name: ExLlamaV3
entries.notes: Use EXL3-specific artifact validation. CPU expert offload is a placement mode, not evidence for standalone CPU execution. TabbyAPI is a serving adapter choice.

entries.name: CTranslate2 / faster-whisper
entries.notes: First adapter faster-whisper. Preserve CTranslate2 identity separately from the Python model implementation. Do not advertise ROCm/Metal.

entries.name: sherpa-onnx
entries.notes: Start CPU recognition/synthesis. Selected GPU/NPU builds and each additional audio operation require their own evidence.

entries.name: MLX-Audio
entries.notes: First target selected Apple Silicon speech models. Share MLX bundle dependencies with MLX-LM where identical, but keep actual worker/accounting ownership.

entries.name: Piper
entries.notes: CPU-first TTS worker through ONNX Runtime, with optional CUDA. Track phonemizer, voice configuration and voice license companions.

entries.name: kokoro-onnx
entries.notes: Alternative to Kokoros, not an alias. First qualify CPU. Additional ONNX providers require this implementation to expose and use them.

entries.name: Text Embeddings Inference
entries.notes: CPU/CUDA first. Metal native execution and supported AMD Instinct ROCm packages have separate platform limits.

entries.name: OpenVINO GenAI
entries.notes: First target selected Intel CPU/GPU text models, then a separately qualified NPU profile. Do not infer every task from the underlying framework.

entries.name: Cactus runtime for Needle / Whistle / Mirage
entries.notes: Start native CPU Needle tool proposals and Whistle recognition. Never execute returned tools in the worker adapter. No inherited cloud fallback. Distinct from cactus-engine.

entries.name: Handy transcribe.cpp
entries.notes: Separate origin from FUTO transcribe.cpp. Choose when a concrete model/streaming requirement is not met by retained speech workers.

entries.name: Cactus Engine general inference SDK
entries.notes: Separate package and bundle identity from current cactus-compute. Disable automatic cloud handoff in managed local profiles.

entries.name: mistral.rs
entries.notes: Select for a concrete model/operation gap. Keep engine libraries in a subprocess worker.

entries.name: Candle
entries.notes: Often a dependency of an implementation such as TEI. Add a standalone adapter only for a named workload.

entries.name: TensorRT-LLM
entries.notes: NVIDIA-specific. Acquire existing prepared models; runtime-owned compiled execution caches must not become model export/quantization tooling.

entries.name: LMDeploy
entries.notes: TurboMind and PyTorch engines are distinct implementation choices with different device and model coverage.

entries.name: KTransformers / KT-Kernel
entries.notes: Heterogeneous MoE expert placement, selected exact models. Can compose with SGLang, so do not automatically create a second serving process or reserve weights twice.

entries.name: MLC-LLM
entries.notes: Use externally prepared target-compatible artifacts. Any required model producer stays outside Juiced's scope.

entries.name: bitnet.cpp
entries.notes: Select compatible BitNet models and published artifacts. CPU implementation and GPU kernel paths are separately qualified.

entries.name: PyTorch / Transformers
entries.notes: Framework dependency, not permission to load arbitrary remote code. A selected model worker defines the actual operation and package boundary.

entries.name: Diffusers
entries.notes: Fixed pipeline IDs and pinned code/models. No generic Python or workflow execution API.

entries.name: Sentence Transformers
entries.notes: PyTorch/ONNX/OpenVINO implementation paths require separate model/runtime identities and output-dimension validation.

entries.name: ONNX Runtime GenAI
entries.notes: Generation layer over ONNX Runtime. Can be a dependency of Ryzen AI OGA, not necessarily another runtime install.

entries.name: WhisperKit / Argmax open-source SDK
entries.notes: Separate WhisperKit/SpeakerKit/TTSKit operation contracts. Open-source and Pro SDK capabilities must not be conflated.

entries.name: FluidAudio
entries.notes: Apple Neural Engine-focused Core ML pipelines. Capture actual stage placement instead of promising all-ANE execution.

entries.name: Vosk
entries.notes: Small-device streaming recognition candidate when its vocabulary/language coverage is needed.

entries.name: NVIDIA NeMo Speech
entries.notes: Use fixed inference workers only. Training, fine-tuning and export remain excluded.

entries.name: Core ML
entries.notes: Usually a dependency of a named implementation. CPU/GPU/ANE compute-unit selection is part of the execution plan.

entries.name: Qualcomm QAIRT / QNN / Genie
entries.notes: Distinguish CPU/Adreno/HTP execution and use selected external prepared models. Keep host firmware/driver ownership outside Juiced.

entries.name: ExecuTorch
entries.notes: Pre-exported .pte and target delegate identity. Some desktop backends are experimental. Never expose torch.export as a Juiced producer.

entries.name: LiteRT / LiteRT-LM
entries.notes: Exact GPU/NPU delegates need target-specific confirmation before selection. Candidate backend names are discovery leads.

entries.name: MNN
entries.notes: Acquire prepared MNN artifacts. Operator/quantization coverage and NPU paths vary by build.

entries.name: ncnn
entries.notes: Named vision/upscaling pipelines. General graph execution and model conversion are outside scope.

entries.name: RKLLM
entries.notes: Rockchip-specific LLM runtime with prepared .rkllm artifacts. Vision companions can require RKNN.

entries.name: RKNN
entries.notes: Selected Rockchip prepared-model pipelines. Separate from RKLLM language execution.

entries.name: HailoRT
entries.notes: Chip family is mandatory. Hailo-8/8L capabilities do not imply Hailo-10 language support, or vice versa.

entries.name: Coral Edge TPU runtime
entries.notes: Compatible precompiled edge vision artifacts and exact USB/PCIe accelerator identity.

entries.name: Ollama
entries.notes: Attach to an explicitly configured service. Observe provider-owned models and lifecycle limits. Do not silently install a second model/cache manager.

entries.name: LM Studio
entries.notes: Attach to its published API. llama.cpp/MLX implementation and actual capabilities must be reported per endpoint/model.

entries.name: KoboldCpp
entries.notes: Attach first. A later managed executable adapter needs one lifecycle owner and selected internal-engine qualification.

entries.name: TabbyAPI
entries.notes: Serving layer for ExLlamaV3. Can serve as its managed worker adapter after qualification, not a duplicate underlying engine.

entries.name: LocalAI
entries.notes: Multi-engine service. Attach with explicit models and operation contracts; do not import its entire backend matrix as Juiced support.

entries.name: ComfyUI
entries.notes: Only explicitly allowed fixed workflows. No arbitrary graph, node install, filesystem or Python execution through public Juiced APIs.

entries.name: llamafile / whisperfile
entries.notes: Distribution of llama.cpp/whisper.cpp. Resolve the embedded build and supported platform before reuse.

entries.name: WebLLM
entries.notes: Browser runs on the client's device, outside daemon resource admission. Requires a separately scoped client-inference design.

entries.name: Transformers.js
entries.notes: Browser ONNX inference is client-local. A server-side Node worker would require a separate managed adapter.

entries.name: ExLlamaV2
entries.notes: Archived upstream. Recognize retained EXL2 installations/artifacts; do not automatically reinterpret them as EXL3.

entries.name: Text Generation Inference
entries.notes: Maintenance mode upstream. Retain attach/import recognition when needed; prefer current engines for new managed integration.
